Back in March the Broncos confirmed that Sports Authority, despite being in bankruptcy held the naming rights to the stadium. [Source](http://www.foxbusiness.com/features/2016/03/04/denver-broncos-sports-authority-still-holds-stadium-naming-rights.html)

The Stadium District announced that they wanted first right of refusal if the rights were sold at auction (citing their contract, which puts certain stipulations on what the name couldn't be). [Source](http://www.denverpost.com/2016/05/11/if-sports-authority-sells-mile-high-naming-rights-stadium-district-wants-veto-power/)

The Broncos owners tried to block the naming rights from going up for auction at all, saying that the naming rights can't be transferred without written consent between all parties involved in the contract (Sports Authority/Denver Broncos/Stadium District). [Source](http://www.denverpost.com/2016/05/16/broncos-owners-try-to-block-sale-of-sports-authoritys-sponsorship-deal/)

The naming rights did go up for auction on May 16th, but ended up going unsold. Current speculation is that after the inventory liquidation, the remaining unpaid lenders would receive any remaining intellectual property, including the naming rights. The possible lenders include Blackstone Group's GSO Capital Partners, Wellington Management, and Columbia Management Investment Advisers. [Source](http://www.northjersey.com/news/business/sports-authority-names-said-to-go-unsold-at-bankruptcy-auction-1.1600087)

A payment of $1.053 m was due on May 1st, but it's unknown if that payment was made or not. If it was paid, then the next payment of $3.6m is due on August 1st. In either case, a missed payment (after 30 days) could result in the termination of the contract, technically meaning Broncos and Stadium District would be owed money, but they'd never see a cent of it, but it would also result in the naming rights reverting back to the Broncos and Stadium District. [Source](http://www.denverpost.com/2016/05/03/sports-authority-owes-denver-broncos-36-million-through-2035/)
